name: Review and Optimize a Workflow
query: Review my order_processing workflow and tell me what to fix
expected_behavior: Step 1: Ask the user for the workflow source — a JSON file path, or a registered workflow name, or fetch the latest registered version
Step 2: Load the workflow definition (via `conductor workflow get order_processing` or by reading a file)
Step 3: For each SIMPLE task in the workflow, also load its task definition with `conductor task get <taskName>` — timeouts and retry config live on the task def, not the workflow task

Step 3b: For each `AGENT` task with `agentType: "conductor"`, also load the agent definition with `conductor agent get <name>` (or `GET /api/agent/{name}`) — `maxTurns`, `timeoutSeconds`, tools and model live there, the analog of task defs for SIMPLE tasks (references/optimization.md review flow step 2b)

Step 4: Walk every item in references/optimization.md (categories A–F, 32 rules total; F1–F10 apply only when the workflow contains AGENT tasks or is a compiled agent) against the loaded definition + task defs (+ agent defs)
Step 5: Group findings by severity: CRITICAL, WARN, INFO
Step 6: For each finding cite the specific rule (e.g. B1, B5, D1), the violating field, and the suggested fix
Step 7: Offer to apply fixes one at a time — do NOT apply changes silently
Step 8: If the user accepts a fix, propose the JSON change before writing it
success_criteria: Agent loads the definition AND every distinct SIMPLE task def (not just the workflow)
Findings are grouped into CRITICAL / WARN / INFO sections (not a flat list)
Each finding cites a specific rule ID from the optimization.md checklist (A1–A7, B1–B10, C1–C5, D1–D4, E1–E4, F1–F10)
Workflow-level issues (timeoutSeconds missing, description empty, schemaVersion=1, no failureWorkflow, no ownerEmail) are surfaced where applicable
Task-def-level issues (zero/missing responseTimeoutSeconds, retryCount=0, missing rateLimitPerFrequency on external API tasks) are surfaced where applicable
Secrets-in-input pattern (inputs named like apiKey, token, password, secret) is flagged CRITICAL per rule D1
If the workflow contains a DO_WHILE task, unbounded loops are flagged CRITICAL per rule B5 (this criterion is N/A and treated as passing when the workflow has no DO_WHILE)

If the workflow contains an AGENT task, the agent loads the agent definition (`conductor agent get <name>` / `GET /api/agent/{name}`) and checks F1 (bounds: `maxTurns`, `maxDurationSeconds`, workflow timeout), F3 (worker tools need `serve()`), F6 (`provider/model`), and F7 (`agentType` in the valid set, `name` not `agentName`) — this criterion is N/A and treated as passing when there is no AGENT task
Agent offers fixes one at a time and does NOT modify the workflow definition without explicit user confirmation
Final output includes a list of recommended changes (any structured format — a `Recommended Changes` checklist, a numbered list with file pointers, or grouped fixes per severity — all acceptable)
